title: fix: return 400 for Trellis validation errors
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- Maps InferencePort HTTP 400 and 422 validation failures to public HTTP 400 for Trellis.
- Keeps authentication, routing, rate-limit, and upstream server failures on their existing paths.
- Adds adapter and worker-level coverage proving invalid image dimensions no longer surface as 502.

## Root cause

The InferencePort client mapped every upstream status except 402 and 429 to 502. InferencePort documents 422 as a request validation error and may return 400 for invalid image properties, so client mistakes polluted official model health.

## Validation

- `npx biome check --write` on changed files
- `npx vitest run test/model3d` (32 tests)
- `npm run typecheck`

gist.headline: Bad dimensions, honest answer
gist.blurb: Trellis now tells you when an image request needs fixing instead of blaming the whole hive. Invalid dimensions get a useful 400, while actual upstream trouble stays on its own path.
gist.summary: Trellis now maps InferencePort's 400 and 422 image-validation responses to public HTTP 400 responses instead of incorrectly returning 502.
gist.impact: Developers submitting invalid image dimensions receive a clear client-error response they can correct, while real auth, routing, rate-limit, and upstream failures keep their existing status handling.

A small CRT monitor robot displays a neat dimension ruler, with code-plants and flowers reinforcing that valid inputs grow into models.
